title: Sets
game_role: When you enter a new region, the places you discovered are listed.
objective: Use sets, collections without duplicates, and do set operations
story: While wandering in the forest, Piko passed the same places again and again. If he writes every visit on his map, the page will fill up! What he really needs is **which places he has seen**, not how many times. Today we meet **sets**, which throw away duplicates by themselves.

sections.title: What is a set?
sections.body:
A set is a collection written with **curly braces** in which **the same item can't appear twice**. The items have no order.

```python
places = {"camp", "village", "camp"}
print(places)       # {'camp', 'village'}  (order may vary)
print(len(places))  # 2
```

To create an empty set, write `set()`. If you write `{}`, you get an empty dictionary.

sections.title: Removing duplicates from a list
sections.body:
Put a list inside `set()` and the duplicates disappear:

```python
visits = ["forest", "village", "forest", "camp"]
unique = set(visits)
print(len(unique))  # 3
```

To see the result in order, use `sorted(unique)`; it gives you an alphabetical list.

sections.title: Add and remove
sections.body:
- `places.add("harbor")` adds an item (nothing happens if it's already there)
- `places.remove("camp")` removes it, and raises an error if it's missing
- `places.discard("camp")` removes it, and quietly moves on if it's missing
- `"village" in places` asks whether it's there, and it's very fast

sections.title: Set operations
sections.body:
Like sets in math, you can compare two sets:

- `a | b` union: everything in both
- `a & b` intersection: what's in both
- `a - b` difference: what's in a but not in b
- `a <= b` is every item of a also in b?

There are word versions too: `a.union(b)`, `a.intersection(b)`, `a.difference(b)`.

examples.title: Duplicates gone
examples.code:
visits = ["forest", "village", "forest", "camp", "village"]
unique = set(visits)
print(len(visits), "visits")
print(len(unique), "different places")
print(sorted(unique))

examples.title: Add and remove
examples.code:
bag = {"sword", "potion"}
bag.add("map")
bag.add("potion")
bag.discard("sword")
print(sorted(bag))
print("potion" in bag)
examples.note: We tried to add the potion twice, but the set has only one.

project_task.title: Discovered places
project_task.prompt:
The places Piko walked through are in the `route` list, and the places he already knew are in the `known` set.

- `visited`: the different places he walked through (a set)
- `new_places`: places he walked through but didn't know before

Then print:

```
4 different places visited
New discoveries: ['cave', 'harbor']
```
project_task.starter:
route = ["camp", "village", "cave", "village", "harbor", "camp"]
known = {"camp", "village"}

# visited and new_places

# print the two lines
project_task.solution:
route = ["camp", "village", "cave", "village", "harbor", "camp"]
known = {"camp", "village"}

visited = set(route)
new_places = visited - known

print(f"{len(visited)} different places visited")
print(f"New discoveries: {sorted(new_places)}")
hints: New places are a difference: visited - known
